To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the first three carotenogenic genes of the car cluster in Myxococccus xanthus, crtE, crIa, and crtB, encode a phytoene‐specific geranygeranyl diphosphate synthase, a CrtI‐phytoene desaturate that is able to dehyrogenate phytoene and cis‐isomerize ζ‐carotenes, and a phytooene synthase.
Myxococcus possesses two phytoene desaturation pathways, each with a different phytoene desaturas, CrtI‐a and Crt I‐b, and that these two desaturases are required for the formation of lycopene.

the phytoene desaturation steps leading to lycopene formation are carried out by two different CrtI‐desaturases, one of which (CrtIa) is capable of isomerizing cis‐phytoene to trans‐phytoene, whereas the second (CrtIb) is not capable of this isomerization, but is capable of desaturating trans‐phytoenes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the carotenoid biosynthetic pathway in M. xanthus, which is the most complex pathway reported to date.
the identification of the genes involved in carotenoid biosynthesis in M. xanthus.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
M. xanthus possesses a phytoene‐to‐lycopene pathway that is composed of two distinct phytoene desaturation steps, the first catalysed by CrtIa, and the second catalysed by the CrtIa–CrtIb complex.

CrtIb is a phytoene dehydrogenase that acts on cis‐phytoene and CrtIa, in addition to being a cis‐to‐ trans isomerase, acts as a phytoene‐ζ‐carotene dehydrogenation enzyme that requires CrtIb to complete lycopene biosynthesis.

M. xanthus uses two different CrtI‐like desaturases that cooperate in the biosynthesis of lycopene, with CrtIa being the first enzyme that dehydrogenates phytoene, and CrtIa also possessing cis‐to‐tran isomerase activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the carB operonic structure of Myxococcus is similar to that found in the plant kingdom, and that the carotene desaturation pathway is similar to the one found in bacteria and plants.
CrtIb is a cis‐to‐cis phytoene desaturation enzyme, and CrtIa has a dual function as a cis‐to ‐trans isomerase and a cis‐to-trans phytoene desatura‐ tion enzyme.
CrtIb is the phytoene‐specific desaturase, whereas Crt Ia is a phytoene/ζ‐carotene‐specific desatrase, and that the two enzymes cooperate to form lycopene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the carotenogenic gene cluster of M. xanthus is more complex than previously believed.

the two CrtI‐like phytoene desaturation genes, crtIa and crtIb, have different substrate specificities and, therefore, they must cooperate to complete the desaturation of phytoene to produce lycopene in M. xanthus.
the carotenogenic gene cluster in M. xanthus is not as simple as it appears to be.
